deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is folio 19 of Grothendieck's 1983 manuscript on the 'Teichmüller tower'. Earlier pages define groupoids of (possibly non-oriented, hence the ±) compact surfaces with boundary. Their objects carry extra data (X, ε or E, R). There is a 'graphe fondamental' attached to such data: a weighted graph with vertices labelled by genus and edges for boundary or gluing circles, presumably with weights. There are 'seven elementary operations' 1°–7°. Earlier pages show that 4° involves restriction and 5° is a gluing or collapsing of circles. The previous page states a 'small dévissage theorem'. Up to equivalence, the whole structure S_A T D^±_typ, with its functors to weighted graphs and to [±1] and its operations 1°–5° (except 4° and 5°), should be reconstructible from the basic groupoids S_1T^±_{g,ν} → T^±_{g,ν} → Ens(ν)×[±1]. These are surfaces of type (g,ν) with marked data on the boundary.

This page states what remains to be done. The essential question is, for a given (rigidified) weighted graph Γ, to construct the groupoid T^±_typ(Γ) of surfaces whose fundamental graph is Γ. One wants this together with its functorial description in Γ and an explicit description of the operations, except 4° and 5°.

The operations of type 4° should come out automatically from the explicit description of T^±_typ(Γ). That description is to be done in the same way as for T^±_{g,ν} and the marked variant ST^±_{g,ν}. Grothendieck then says a further operation (read 'bordage', probably 'bouchage/bouclage' = capping off boundary circles) could be made explicit using its special cases for ST_{g,ν} and T_{g,ν}. These special cases should be made 'standard', i.e. 'elementary'.

He writes the elementary case as (**): ST^±_{g,ν,ν'} → ST_{g,ν⊔ν'}. Here the source consists of surfaces X of type (g,ν), or of type (g,ν⊔ν'), equipped with a subset I' ⊂ I(X) of boundary components of cardinality ν', namely those to be capped. In modern terms this is the capping map relating mapping class groupoids of surfaces with different numbers of boundary components at fixed genus. On the group level it is the Birman/capping exact sequence.

Margins: 'avec ou sans S?' asks whether the boundary marking S should be kept in this operation. 'NB on laisse ici D, S en dehors du contexte des Γ' says that the D and S decorations are set aside in the graph-indexed setting.

The next page notes the limitation of these capping operations: they never relate T_{g,ν} to lower genus. That requires operation 5°, gluing or collapsing the former gluing circles. It then turns to fundamental groupoids Π_1(X;R) with base points in R.

Overall purpose: organise all mapping class groupoids into a tower indexed by stable graphs Γ, with functoriality in Γ and gluing, capping and restriction operations. This is the 1983 prehistory of the 'Teichmüller tower / Lego' of Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: No mathematical error can be checked: the page is a programme statement, not a proof.

Minor ambiguity: the arrow in (**) goes from the (g,ν,ν') groupoid to the (g,ν⊔ν') groupoid, while the explanatory note describes objects of type (g,ν) with a subset I' of the boundary. The indexing of ν versus ν⊔ν' is not consistent as written. The intended source is presumably surfaces of type (g,ν⊔ν') with ν' marked components, and the map that forgets or caps them.
The claim that the 4° operations come 'automatically' from the explicit description of T_typ(Γ) is asserted without argument.

ideas.what: Groupoid T^±_typ(Γ) of (possibly non-orientable) surfaces with prescribed combinatorial type given by a weighted dual graph Γ, described functorially in Γ
ideas.modern_name: Mapping class groupoids indexed by stable graphs; boundary strata of M̄_{g,n}; modular operad structure on mapping class groupoids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984) for the tower idea; formalised by Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998) and Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (2000)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §§ on the Teichmüller tower and 'jeu de Lego', in spirit; not with this ± graph-indexed formalism

ideas.what: Capping (bouchage) of a chosen subset I' of boundary components as an elementary operation ST_{g,ν⊔ν'} → ST_{g,ν}
ideas.modern_name: Capping homomorphism / Birman exact sequence for mapping class groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birman (1969) and standard mapping class group theory

ideas.what: Reduction of the whole tower structure to basic pieces T_{g,ν} plus elementary operations (a 'dévissage')
ideas.modern_name: Generators-and-relations / Lego presentation of the Teichmüller tower
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (statement that the tower is generated by low-modular-dimension pieces)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out to build the full functor Γ ↦ T^±_typ(Γ), including non-orientable surfaces (±) and boundary markings S, together with explicit compatibilities with seven operations. The non-orientable (±) version of the graph-indexed tower with capping is less developed in the later literature than the orientable modular-operad version.
missed.quote: La question essentielle reste en somme de construire, pour un graphe pondéré ... Γ, le groupoïde T^±_typ(Γ), avec sa description fonctorielle en Γ, et l'explicitation des sept opérations
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Non-orientable versions of the Teichmüller tower and Grothendieck–Teichmüller actions (e.g. via real moduli spaces) are an active but thinner area. This is a modest pointer, not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a programmatic to-do note inside the 1983 Teichmüller-tower manuscript. It anticipates what became Esquisse's Lego/tower and modular-operad structures, which are already credited to Grothendieck in spirit. The only slightly distinctive feature is the systematic inclusion of non-orientable (±) surfaces and boundary markings, but no concrete result is stated.
transcription_corrections: Subscript is 'typ' (as on previous page: T^±_typ(Γ)), not 'top'.
Line 2 likely reads 'de construire, pour un graphe pondéré' (or 'bipondéré'), not 'graphe fondamental'.
'bordage' is more likely 'bouchage' or 'bouclage', consistent with 'opérations de bouclage' on the next page.
The '$' symbol is Grothendieck's barred S (the marked/S-decorated groupoid ST), not a dollar sign.
Left margin: 'NB on laisse ici "D", "S" en dehors du contexte des Γ' (approximately).
